    }
    .fake-h2 {

        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
        display: block;
    }
    .card-description {
        color: #6b7280;
        font-size: 0.95rem;
    }
    #concept-map {
        width: 100%;
        height: 800px;
        cursor: grab;
        background: #fcfcfc;
    }

    .node circle {

    }

    .link.link-main { stroke-width: 3px; stroke: #6b7280; stroke-opacity: 0.8; }
    
    .tooltip {

<div class="concept-container">
    <div class="map-card">
        <div class="map-header">
            <span class="fake-h2">My Personal Learning Theory</span>
             <div class="legend">
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #eab308;"></div><span class="legend-label">Behaviorism</span></div>
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #22c55e;"></div><span class="legend-label">Cognitivism</span></div>
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #3b82f6;"></div><span class="legend-label">Constructivism</span></div>
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #f97316;"></div><span class="legend-label">Social Learning</span></div>
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #ec4899;"></div><span class="legend-label">Neuroscience</span></div>
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #64748b;"></div><span class="legend-label">Educational Tech</span></div>
            <div class="legend-item"><div class="legend-color" style="background: #ef4444;"></div><span class="legend-label">Connectivism</span></div>
        </div>
            <p class="card-description"> • Press and hold the purple bubble to auto-sort • Scroll to zoom • Click and drag to move</p>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
            <svg id="concept-map"></svg>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

<div class="tooltip" id="tooltip">
    <div class="tooltip-title" id="tooltip-title"></div>
    <div class="tooltip-description" id="tooltip-description"></div>
</div>

<script is:inline src="https://d3js.org/d3.v7.min.js"></script>

<script is:inline>
    // D3.js Concept Map Logic
    const graphData = {
        nodes: [
            { id: "personal-theory", label: "My Personal Learning Theory", group: "personal", size: 60, description: "My learning theory weaves together social interaction, hands-on knowledge building, behavioral strategies, and explicit metacognitive instruction." },
            { id: "behaviorism", label: "Behaviorism", group: "behaviorism", size: 30, description: "Utilizing reinforcement strategies to shape foundational skills before progressing to complex cognitive challenges." },
            { id: "cognitivism", label: "Cognitivism", group: "cognitivism", size: 30, description: "Frameworks helping students develop internal skills of reflection and problem-solving." },
            { id: "constructivism-main", label: "Constructivism", group: "constructivism", size: 30, description: "Prioritizing student autonomy through social and collaborative contexts." },
            { id: "social-learning-main", label: "Social Learning Theory", group: "social", size: 30, description: "Fostering self-efficacy through modeling, observation, and situated learning." },
            { id: "neuroscience", label: "Neuroscience", group: "neuroscience", size: 30, description: "Leveraging attention and emotion to transform information into consolidated neural networks." },
            { id: "technological", label: "Educational Technology", group: "technological", size: 30, description: "Amplify teaching via tools that empower interactive, personalized learning." },
            { id: "connectivism", label: "Connectivism", group: "connectivism", size: 30, description: "Learning is most effective when information is meaningfully distributed across networks." },
            // Sub-nodes
            { id: "distributed-knowledge", label: "Distributed Knowledge", group: "connectivism", size: 8 },
            { id: "pavlov", label: "Pavlov", group: "behaviorism", size: 10 },
            { id: "skinner", label: "Skinner", group: "behaviorism", size: 10 },
            { id: "classical-cond", label: "Classical Conditioning", group: "behaviorism", size: 8 },
            { id: "operant-cond", label: "Operant Conditioning", group: "behaviorism", size: 8 },
            { id: "reinforcement", label: "Reinforcement", group: "behaviorism", size: 8 },
            { id: "consequences-behav", label: "Consequences", group: "behaviorism", size: 8 },
            { id: "piaget-cog", label: "Piaget (Cog)", group: "cognitivism", size: 10 },
            { id: "working-memory", label: "Working Memory", group: "cognitivism", size: 8 },
            { id: "long-term-memory", label: "Long-Term Memory", group: "cognitivism", size: 8 },
            { id: "schema", label: "Schema", group: "cognitivism", size: 8 },
            { id: "vygotsky", label: "Vygotsky", group: "constructivism", size: 10 },
            { id: "zpd", label: "ZPD", group: "constructivism", size: 8 },
            { id: "collaboration", label: "Collaboration", group: "constructivism", size: 8 },
            { id: "modeling", label: "Modeling", group: "social", size: 8 },
            { id: "situated-cognition", label: "Situated Cognition", group: "social", size: 10 },
            { id: "neuroplasticity", label: "Neuroplasticity", group: "neuroscience", size: 8 },
            { id: "ai-in-education", label: "AI in Education", group: "technological", size: 10 },
            { id: "immersive-learning", label: "AR/VR/MR", group: "technological", size: 10 },
        ],
        links: [
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "behaviorism", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "cognitivism", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "constructivism-main", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "social-learning-main", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "neuroscience", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "technological", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "personal-theory", target: "connectivism", distance: 60, class: "link-main" },
            { source: "behaviorism", target: "pavlov" },
            { source: "behaviorism", target: "skinner" },
            { source: "pavlov", target: "classical-cond" },
            { source: "skinner", target: "operant-cond" },
            { source: "cognitivism", target: "piaget-cog" },
            { source: "cognitivism", target: "schema" },
            { source: "constructivism-main", target: "vygotsky" },
            { source: "vygotsky", target: "zpd" },
            { source: "technological", target: "ai-in-education" },
            { source: "neuroscience", target: "neuroplasticity" },
        ]
    };

    const colorMap = {
        "personal": "#a855f7", "behaviorism": "#eab308", "cognitivism": "#22c55e",
        "constructivism": "#3b82f6", "social": "#f97316", "neuroscience": "#ec4899",
        "technological": "#64748b", "connectivism": "#ef4444"
    };

    const svg = d3.select("#concept-map");
    const container = svg.node().parentElement;
    const width = container.clientWidth;
    const height = 800;
    svg.attr("width", width).attr("height", height);
    const g = svg.append("g");

    const simulation = d3.forceSimulation(graphData.nodes)
        .force("link", d3.forceLink(graphData.links).id(d => d.id).distance(100))
        .force("charge", d3.forceManyBody().strength(-300))
        .force("center", d3.forceCenter(width / 2, height / 2))
        .force("collision", d3.forceCollide().radius(d => d.size * 2));

    const link = g.append("g").selectAll("line")
        .data(graphData.links).join("line")
        .attr("class", d => d.class ? `link ${d.class}` : "link");

    const node = g.append("g").selectAll("g")
        .data(graphData.nodes).join("g")
        .attr("class", "node")
        .call(d3.drag().on("start", (e, d) => {
            if (!e.active) simulation.alphaTarget(0.3).restart();
            d.fx = d.x; d.fy = d.y;
        }).on("drag", (e, d) => {
            d.fx = e.x; d.fy = e.y;
        }).on("end", (e, d) => {
            if (!e.active) simulation.alphaTarget(0);
            d.fx = null; d.fy = null;
        }));

    node.append("circle").attr("r", d => d.size).attr("fill", d => colorMap[d.group]);
    node.append("text").text(d => d.label).attr("dy", "0.35em");

    simulation.on("tick", () => {
        link.attr("x1", d => d.source.x).attr("y1", d => d.source.y)
            .attr("x2", d => d.target.x).attr("y2", d => d.target.y);
        node.attr("transform", d => `translate(${d.x},${d.y})`);
    });

    svg.call(d3.zoom().on("zoom", (e) => g.attr("transform", e.transform)));
</script>

<div class="reflection-dropdown">
  <div class="dropdown-item">
    <div class="dropdown-question">Reflection</div>
    <div class="dropdown-answer">
      <p><strong>Tool Selection and Rationale</strong><br><br>
      For my concept map, I chose to use the D3.js library to create an interactive, force-directed graph. I wanted to move beyond static mind-maps to show the constantly shifting relationship between theories. D3.js allows concepts to pull on and repel each other through physics, which I found illustrative of my personal learning journey.</p>

      <p><strong>Reflection and Learning</strong><br><br>
      While not perfect, I am happy with the choice to try something new. Creating this map reinforces the idea that the learning process is messy, dynamic, and relational.</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>

<script is:inline>
  document.querySelectorAll('.dropdown-question').forEach(q => {
    q.addEventListener('click', () => q.parentElement.classList.toggle('active'));
  });
</script>
